title: The Prediction Archive - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: The Prediction Archive is a public AI-built database of tens of thousands of world predictions spanning decades, marked to market, and it currently ranks Alex Tabarrok the highest individual predictor in the world. Ranking uses the Wilson score, so volume of predictions counts alongside accuracy, and the author expects his own rank to fall as coverage expands.

insights.claim: The Prediction Archive is a public database of tens of thousands of world predictions that uses AI to track predictions across many decades and mark them to market.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: A new public dataset for auditing pundit and forecaster track records — useful for deciding whose macro calls deserve weight.
insights.quote: The Prediction Archive is a public database of tens of thousands of world predictions.
insights.locator: The Prediction Archive is a public database

insights.claim: Rankings in the archive are based on the Wilson score, so a forecaster gets credit not just for accuracy but for making enough predictions to shrink uncertainty about that accuracy.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Scoring methodology determines the leaderboard: high-accuracy, low-volume forecasters are penalized, which changes how you read any track-record ranking.
insights.locator: Ranks are based on the Wilson score

insights.claim: Under Wilson scoring Bryan Caplan was more accurate but makes fewer predictions, and Tyler Cowen made many more predictions while being only somewhat less accurate — so volume, not raw hit rate, drives the top of the leaderboard.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Named comparisons let you calibrate how much to trust specific public commentators' forecasts.
insights.locator: Bryan Caplan was more accurate than I was

insights.claim: What the AI classifies as a 'prediction' sometimes reflects commentary on contemporary events rather than genuine forecasts, so the archive's accuracy numbers should be discounted, and rankings are expected to shift as the archive expands.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Early leaderboard positions are unstable; do not treat current rankings as a settled measure of forecasting skill.
insights.quote: What the AI marks as predictions seem sometimes to be more about contemporary events, so take the numbers with a grain of salt.
insights.locator: What the AI marks as predictions

insights.claim: Coverage of the archive extends to public macro and markets commentators including Peter Zeihan, Scott Alexander and Warren Buffett.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Gives a way to score the hit rate of widely-followed geopolitical and investing voices rather than relying on their self-reported records.
insights.locator: Other people the archive covers include
